capsule-101.k1: An OTP is a one-time password sent to your phone. No legitimate company, agent, or relative should ever ask for it. If someone does, it is a scam.
capsule-101.k2: Check the domain before tapping. The real GCash is at gcash.com. Fake links often end in .help, .xyz, or .top, or misspell the company name.
capsule-101.k3: DSWD does not charge a fee and does not ask for an OTP to release aid. If someone asks for a payment or an OTP to release help, it is a scam.
capsule-101.k4: A screenshot is not proof of a transfer. Open the app and check your balance before sending any money back.
capsule-101.k5: If you suddenly lose signal, cannot make calls, and OTPs stop arriving, a SIM swap may be in progress. Call your network provider immediately from another phone.
capsule-101.k6: Before paying by QR, check the recipient name in the app. If it does not match who you expect, cancel the payment.
capsule-101.k7: Use a random PIN that is not a birthday, not 1234, and never posted on social media. Change it if you suspect someone knows it.
capsule-101.k8: If you are scammed, change your PIN immediately, report it in the app, call the hotline, and screenshot the conversation before blocking the sender. The first 30 minutes matter most.
capsule-101.k9: The sender name on a text message can be faked. A name like GCash or a logo proves nothing. Check the number and never tap the link.
capsule-101.k10: A photo of your ID can be used to open an account in your name. Blur the ID number and never post it publicly.
capsule-101.k11: A legitimate wallet lists its fees inside the app, never in a text message. If someone texts you to pay a fee to release money, it is a scam.
capsule-101.k12: If your account is hacked, use the official recovery flow in the app and the hotline. Never pay anyone offering a recovery service on social media.

capsule-102.k1: An online job is work done with a phone or laptop and internet: virtual assistant, transcription, social media manager, or data entry. Many entry-level gigs need no degree.
capsule-102.k2: No legitimate employer asks for a registration fee, training fee, or load. If you must pay to work, it is a scam.
capsule-102.k3: One clear photo, one line about your skill, and one way to contact you. That is all you need to start.
capsule-102.k4: Fake job posts offer very high pay, require no experience, and ask for a fee. A real employer states the scope and the working hours.
capsule-102.k5: Before applying, make one sample that matches the job: a spreadsheet, a transcription sample, or a simple graphic. That is what you show instead of experience.
capsule-102.k6: Apply to three to five jobs a day and track where you applied. Most will not reply, and that is normal.
capsule-102.k7: Before starting, agree on scope, hours, and payment. If the work grows, agree on the new rate before continuing.
capsule-102.k8: No legitimate employer asks for your OTP for verification. Refuse and report the person asking.
capsule-102.k9: Use a traceable payment method such as a bank transfer or a wallet with a record. Avoid payments with no receipt or trail.
capsule-102.k10: In an online interview, ask about scope, hours, and payment. Be careful if they refuse to answer.
capsule-102.k11: If an employer scams you, report and block them, and screenshot the evidence. Do not pay more to recover what you lost.
capsule-102.k12: For your first client, start with a small task and a clear deadline. Good communication matters more than a fancy portfolio.

capsule-103.k1: Digital literacy is the ability to find, check, and use information and apps safely. It is not measured by the price of your phone.
capsule-103.k2: When searching, use specific keywords and add the place or the year. Open two results and compare them before believing either one.
capsule-103.k3: Check who wrote a post and when it was published. Cross-check a second trustworthy source, and be wary of shocking posts and AI-generated images.
capsule-103.k4: Install apps from Google Play only. A simple app should not ask for SMS, contacts, or your ID.
capsule-103.k5: Permissions should match what the app does. Refuse access it does not need and uninstall apps you no longer use.
capsule-103.k6: Use a long passphrase that you do not reuse on any other account, and never share it with anyone.
capsule-103.k7: Two-step verification adds a second code or approval that protects the account even if the password leaks.
capsule-103.k8: A signed-in Google account backs up contacts and photos. Keep recovery codes offline, outside the phone.
capsule-103.k9: Delete unused media, install system updates, and avoid cleaner apps that promise speed.
capsule-103.k10: Look for unnatural details in an image and find the original source before believing or sharing it.
capsule-103.k11: A screenshot of your ID can be used to open accounts in your name. Blur the number and never post it publicly.
capsule-103.k12: Download lessons on Wi-Fi and use them offline. Limit video streaming when you are on mobile data.

capsule-104.k1: Track every expense for 30 days, including the small ones, so you can see where the money really goes.
capsule-104.k2: Needs come first. Wants are optional and are the first thing to cut when income is short.
capsule-104.k3: The 50/30/20 split is a guide for needs, wants, and savings, not a rule that fits every income.
capsule-104.k4: Divide your cash into labeled envelopes so each category has a hard limit.
capsule-104.k5: Set savings aside before you spend, even a small amount, as long as it is regular. Keep it in a separate wallet or container.
capsule-104.k6: Target three to six months of needs. Start with one week, and keep the fund separate but easy to reach.
capsule-104.k7: Compare the total repayment, not just the weekly installment. Informal 5-6 lending is expensive and the debt grows fast.
capsule-104.k8: Before borrowing, write down the amount, the interest, the due date, and the payment schedule. Check that your income can carry the monthly payment.
capsule-104.k9: Guaranteed high returns, urgency, and referral bonuses are red flags. A legitimate investment carries risk and paperwork.
capsule-104.k10: Check an offer against the SEC list of registered entities before paying. Registration is not a promise of profit, but it is a sign of a legitimate company.
capsule-104.k11: Save a little each month for known future costs such as school fees and Christmas, so they do not become debt.
capsule-104.k12: Review the budget every month and adjust the categories when they do not fit. Do not throw the plan away and start over.

capsule-105.k1: Family planning is deciding whether to have a child, when, and how many, including health and fertility awareness.
capsule-105.k2: A plan helps parents care for their children and reduces unplanned pregnancies.
capsule-105.k3: At least two years between births helps the mother recover. Ask a health worker.
capsule-105.k4: The calendar, LAM, and BBT are natural methods that need correct use and a partner's cooperation. LAM has strict conditions.
capsule-105.k5: LAM works only with exclusive breastfeeding, no period, and a baby under six months.
capsule-105.k6: Condoms are the method that also protects against HIV and other STIs when used correctly.
capsule-105.k7: Pills, injectables, and implants are effective when used correctly. Side effects vary from person to person.
capsule-105.k8: An IUD lasts for years. BTL and vasectomy are permanent.
capsule-105.k9: Barangay health centers, RHUs, and public hospitals provide information and services.
capsule-105.k10: The Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act guarantees access to family planning information and services.
capsule-105.k11: Pills do not cause permanent infertility, condoms are effective with correct use, and vasectomy does not lower libido.
capsule-105.k12: Decisions are voluntary, both partners are respected, and side effects are reported to a health worker.

capsule-106.k1: Inventory is a record of stock, quantity, and value. It shows what sells and what is missing.
capsule-106.k2: Write the item, unit cost, selling price, stock in, stock out, balance, and expiry on the stock card.
capsule-106.k3: Record every stock movement the same day, even small withdrawals.
capsule-106.k4: The reorder point is average daily sales times lead time, plus safety stock.
capsule-106.k5: The extra stock you keep covers delivery delays and sudden demand.
capsule-106.k6: Sell older stock first, check dates weekly, and pull out expired items.
capsule-106.k7: Breakage, spoilage, and missing items are losses and must be recorded right away.
capsule-106.k8: Gross profit is sales minus the cost of the goods sold.
capsule-106.k9: Keep store cash apart from household cash and record the owner's withdrawals.
capsule-106.k10: Bundle, discount, or stop reordering items that do not sell.
capsule-106.k11: Know the supplier's delivery days, minimum order, and credit terms before ordering.
capsule-106.k12: Review a month of sales to decide what to reorder and what to drop.
